url.description: The pattern is the real check; format: "uri" is not evaluated without a FormatChecker.

domain.description: The registrable domain (eTLD+1) of `url`, lowercase, no port and no trailing dot — blog.foo.com and foo.com must both be stored as foo.com. Gate 3 counts distinct values of this field to measure source independence, so a host stored unreduced silently defeats it. Produce it with scripts/domains.py:registrable(); the pattern here only rejects strings that are not hostname-shaped at all, it cannot tell an unreduced host from a reduced one.

quote.description: The verbatim span, byte-for-byte as the extractor copied it. The pattern requires 8 characters that are neither whitespace nor zero-width — evidence.MIN_QUOTE_CHARS, the same bar schemas/artifact.extract.json enforces at gate 1 and apply_extract enforces in code before it writes a citation. Not gate 2: gate 2 is the rechecker subagent's judgement now, outside this process, so nothing in this codebase enforces a length there. A shorter span is a substring of almost any page, so a re-check confirming it would not be evidence; storing one as a citation is what let three artifacts quoting "a" reach `supported`.

quote_sha256.description: sha256 of the NORMALIZED quote (evidence.normalize), not of the raw `quote` field. The hash is a span's identity, and spec section 2 requires that one source cited by twelve facts is stored once — which only holds if the same sentence quoted with different line wrapping produces the same hash. `quote` itself stays byte-verbatim.

http_status.description: Not every server answers with a real HTTP status: LinkedIn returns 999. The cap was 599, which made such a response a PERMANENT tick wedge — memory.create raised out of submit, and because the value is deterministic every retry died on the same line with no repair path. Recorded as sent rather than clamped, because a clamped value is a lie about what the server did. Currently always null: gate 2 is the rechecker subagent's judgement now, not an HTTP client, so nothing in this codebase observes a status code to record. Kept, required and nullable, for schema compatibility.

source_type.description: The `source_type` the extractor reported. Recorded and reported, NOT gated. Gate 3 counts distinct registrable domains, and two of them can still be one source - a syndicated release, or two posts citing one paper. Detecting that needs origin identification, which is fuzzy matching over model-reported attributions and wrong too often for promotion to rest on. Gating on `primary` instead fails the other way: a question whose honest literature is all secondary would never promote anything. So the report DISCLOSES a claim carried entirely by non-primary sources and leaves the judgement to the reader. OPTIONAL, absent meaning written before this field existed - citation.json is additionalProperties: false and page_sha256's description costs out what a required addition does.

published_at.description: When the SOURCE was published, as the page states it -- not when we read it. `fetched_at` is written by apply_recheck and is the date gate 2 re-read the page, so before this field the only date the bibliography could print was our own. A reader could not tell a 2011 page from a 2025 one. Partial dates are legal (2019, 2019-03, 2019-03-04) because many pages give only a year and demanding a full date would make the extractor invent a month and a day. `null` is a first-class answer and the ordinary one for a page carrying no date, or carrying only a misleading `last updated` banner: an invented date in a bibliography is worse than an honest gap. OPTIONAL, absent meaning `written before this field existed` -- required, it would invalidate every citation already on disk, exactly as page_sha256 below records. Nothing acts on this value; it is recorded and reported, not used to prefer or demote a source.

page_sha256.description: Nothing writes this any more. It used to hold the sha256 of the normalized page text gate 2 read — the file at evidence/<id>.raw.txt — so a later re-fetch could tell 'the page changed' from 'the quote was never there'. Gate 2 is the rechecker subagent's judgement now, that httpx pipeline is deleted, and no writer produces the field. Kept, optional, purely so a store written BEFORE gate 2 became a subagent still validates: this schema is additionalProperties: false and the pre-branch apply_extract wrote page_sha256 on every citation it created, so dropping the field did not just stop new writes — it made every citation already on disk schema-invalid, which drops it out of live_citations (a verified citation vanishes), rescores its hypotheses to 0, and makes apply._citation_is_gone quarantine its facts on the first submit after the upgrade. Those demotions are irreversible: promotion only happens when a fresh verify verdict lands. Absent means 'written by the current writer', exactly as absent cascaded means false in schemas/assumption.json.
